newsitem.title: USA: American pilots propose regional contracts bargaining.
newsitem.headline: American pilots propose regional contracts bargaining.

text.p: American Airlines pilots late on Wednesday told American negotiators they would bargain on a key issue to avert a looming strike, a union source close to the negotiations said early on Thursday morning.
The source said the pilots proposed to bargain on the compensation package given to pilots, who will fly new, high-tech, commuter regional jets that may hit runways next year.

The source told reporters this was a significant step toward a compromise to avert a pilots' strike set for midnight on Friday (0500 GMT). "There's no bluff, there's no smoke here," the source, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said.
Under the pilot's proposal, the new commuter flights would be flown under the banner of American Airlines, not as American Eagle as is planned by the number-two U.S. carrier.

The source said the pilots are willing to negotiate on the commuter jet package for pilots regarding pay and work rules, but not on pension, benefits nor vacation time. The source also said that the pilots union, the Allied Pilots Association, is requesting that the new commuter jets make up only 20 percent of American's total jet fleet.

American has proposed that the jets be flown by lower paid members of another union. "We're asking for a higher rate to operate a new aircraft that is more capable and more efficient," the source said.
The source said American had not yet responded to the proposal, and American president Donald Carty told reporters as he left the negotiations at a Washington hotel that he had not seen a proposal.
